    # In openpyxl, standard yellow is often 'FFFF00'.

    is_yellow = False

        # Check for common yellow RGB values (Standard Yellow)
        # Some Excel files use 'FFFF00' or 'FFFFFF00'
        if fill.start_color.rgb in ['FFFF00', 'FFFFFF00']:
            is_yellow = True

        current_value = cell.value
        if current_value is not None:
            # The instruction says to add prefix "//" to the pattern.
            # Example: ["/out/", ...] -> //[ ["/out/", ...]
            # Since the value already starts with "[", adding "//" results in "//[".
            cell.value = "//" + str(current_value)

# Save the workbook
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)",
